figurative_meaning_bn: হিন্দু পুরাণোক্ত প্রবল বিদ্বেষভাবাপন্ন দুই সহোদর মুনিকুমার
figurative_meaning_en: Two brother sages harboring intense enmity, as mentioned in Hindu Puranas
example_sentences_in_bangla: তাদের সম্পর্ক গজকচ্ছপের মতো, সর্বদা বিদ্বেষে ভরা।
ভাইদের মধ্যে গজকচ্ছপের প্রতিদ্বন্দিতা দেখে সকলে দুঃখিত।
example_sentences_in_english: Their relationship is like Gajakachchhapa, always filled with enmity.
The brothers' rivalry resembles Gajakachchhapa, causing sorrow to everyone.
history: Refers to the Puranic tale of two brother sages who, due to a curse, were reborn as an elephant and a tortoise, symbolizing their perpetual and intense mutual hatred.
note: This idiom draws from Hindu mythological narratives, emphasizing familial discord rooted in ancient lore.
